**Known hazards for future sprints:**
- Direct SqliteSlopeStore construction bypasses resolveStore and must explicitly resolve repository state ownership.
- Generated worktrees must never copy or symlink .slope state; git common-dir ownership is the only supported sharing mechanism.
- Porcelain status parsing must preserve the two-character status column, including a leading space for unstaged changes.

### Training Log

| Type | Description | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Lessons | A shared-state migration must inventory direct constructors, maintenance commands, generated worktrees, initialization paths, and compatibility registries, not only the central store factory. | S261 now has command-level actual-git coverage across those entry points. |
| Lessons | Repository ownership and nested project discovery are related but distinct: linked worktrees adopt the primary owner, while an explicit nested SLOPE project keeps its own state. | The resolver and MCP discovery tests cover both descendants of nested projects and legacy copied configs at linked-worktree roots. |
